subjects.name: Indian GK
subjects.desc: States, symbols, rivers and the basics every Indian learner should know.

questions.q: What is the capital of India?
questions.e: New Delhi has been India's capital since 1911, when it replaced Kolkata.

questions.q: Which is the national animal of India?
questions.e: The Royal Bengal Tiger was declared the national animal in 1973.

questions.q: Which river is the longest in India?
questions.e: The Ganga flows about 2,525 km within India, longer than any other Indian river.

questions.q: How many states does India have today?
questions.e: India has 28 states and 8 union territories.

questions.q: Who is called the Father of the Nation in India?
questions.e: Mahatma Gandhi is called the Father of the Nation for leading the freedom movement.

questions.q: Which is the national bird of India?
questions.e: The Indian peacock was declared the national bird in 1963.

questions.q: Who wrote India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.e: Rabindranath Tagore wrote both 'Jana Gana Mana' and 'Amar Sonar Bangla'.

questions.q: In which year did India become independent?
questions.e: India became independent on 15 August 1947.

questions.q: Which city is known as the Pink City?
questions.e: Jaipur is called the Pink City because of its terracotta-pink buildings.

questions.q: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.e: Rajasthan covers about 3.42 lakh square km, the largest of any state.

questions.q: The Constitution of India came into effect on which date?
questions.e: It came into force on 26 January 1950, now celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru took office on 15 August 1947.

questions.q: Which is the smallest state of India by area?
questions.e: Goa is the smallest state by area, at about 3,702 square km.

questions.q: Which state is called the 'Land of Five Rivers'?
questions.e: Punjab takes its name from 'panj ab' — five rivers.

questions.q: Which mountain range separates India from Tibet?
questions.e: The Himalayas form the northern boundary between India and the Tibetan plateau.

questions.q: Which city is called the Silicon Valley of India?
questions.e: Bengaluru is called so because of its large IT and startup industry.

questions.q: Which is India's national flower?
questions.e: The lotus was declared the national flower in 1950.

questions.q: What is the currency of India?
questions.e: The Indian rupee is issued by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution guarantees equality before the law?
questions.e: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.

questions.q: Which is the largest inland salt lake in India?
questions.e: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland salt lake.

subjects.name: Science & Nature
subjects.desc: Body, plants, chemistry and the everyday science behind the world.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.e: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom make water.

questions.q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air?
questions.e: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.q: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
questions.e: An adult human body has 206 bones; babies are born with about 270.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.e: The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.

questions.q: Which part of the cell is called the powerhouse?
questions.e: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's energy.

questions.q: Which vitamin does the skin make from sunlight?
questions.e: Sunlight on the skin helps the body produce vitamin D.

questions.q: Which is the hardest natural substance?
questions.e: Diamond ranks 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.e: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum'. Ag is silver.

questions.q: What is the pH of pure water?
questions.e: Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7.

questions.q: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.e: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.

questions.q: What does DNA stand for?
questions.e: DNA carries the genetic instructions for living things.

questions.q: Which part of a plant makes food?
questions.e: Leaves make food through photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.e: Chickenpox is viral. Malaria is caused by a parasite, cholera by bacteria, ringworm by fungus.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.e: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.q: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.e: Skin is the body's largest organ by surface area and weight.

questions.q: Which acid gives lemons their sour taste?
questions.e: Lemons contain citric acid.

questions.q: What is the process by which plants make food?
questions.e: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make glucose.

questions.q: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.e: O negative blood can be given to almost any patient.

questions.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.e: Light travels about 3,00,000 km every second in a vacuum.

questions.q: Which organ filters waste from the blood?
questions.e: The kidneys filter waste and excess water into urine.

subjects.name: AI & Technology
subjects.desc: AI basics, how the internet works and staying safe online.

questions.q: What does AI stand for?
questions.e: AI means Artificial Intelligence.

questions.q: What does 'LLM' stand for in AI?
questions.e: ChatGPT and similar tools are built on large language models.

questions.q: What is a 'prompt' in AI?
o: The instruction you give the AI
questions.e: A prompt is the text or instruction the AI responds to.

questions.q: What does 'GPU' stand for?
questions.e: GPUs handle the heavy maths that AI models need.

questions.q: What is machine learning?
o: Systems that learn patterns from data
questions.e: Machine learning models improve by finding patterns in data.

questions.q: Which company developed ChatGPT?
questions.e: OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022.

questions.q: What does 'URL' stand for?
questions.e: A URL is the address of a page on the web.

questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.e: Long, random, mixed-character passwords are hardest to guess.

questions.q: What is phishing?
o: Fake messages that try to steal your details
questions.e: Phishing pretends to be a trusted source to get passwords or OTPs.

questions.q: What does 'cloud storage' mean?
o: Files saved on your phone only
questions.e: Cloud files live on remote servers and are accessed over the internet.

questions.q: How many megabytes are in one gigabyte?
questions.e: 1 GB = 1024 MB in binary measurement.

questions.q: What is the job of HTML?
questions.e: HTML defines the structure and content of a web page.

questions.q: In AI, what is a 'hallucination'?
questions.e: AI models can invent facts that sound convincing but are false.

questions.q: What does 'open source' mean?
questions.e: Open source means anyone can read, use and modify the code.

questions.q: Which of these is an AI image-generation tool?
questions.e: Midjourney generates images from text prompts.

questions.q: What is two-factor authentication?
o: A second verification step after your password
questions.e: 2FA adds an OTP or app code on top of your password.

questions.q: What does 'CPU' stand for?
questions.e: The CPU is the main processor of a computer.

questions.q: What is a VPN mainly used for?
questions.e: A VPN encrypts your traffic and hides your IP address.

questions.q: In AI models, what is a 'token' roughly?
o: A chunk of text the model processes
questions.e: Models read and generate text in small pieces called tokens.

questions.q: Which of these is the safest way to share an OTP?
o: With a caller who asks for it
With a bank official over phone
questions.e: No bank, company or government office will ask for your OTP.

subjects.name: English Grammar & Vocabulary
subjects.desc: Grammar rules, tenses and the words that make writing clearer.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: She ___ to school every day.
questions.e: With he/she/it in the present simple, add -s: she goes.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
questions.e: 'Children' is an irregular plural.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'happy'?
questions.e: Joyful and happy both mean feeling pleasure.

questions.q: What is the opposite of 'ancient'?
questions.e: Ancient means very old; modern means of the present time.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct?
questions.e: Necessary: one c, two s's.

questions.q: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.e: We say 'good at' a skill or subject.

questions.q: What is the past tense of 'go'?
questions.e: 'Go' is irregular: go, went, gone.

questions.q: Which of these is a noun?
questions.e: Beauty is a thing (noun); beautiful is an adjective.

questions.q: I have lived here ___ 2010.
questions.e: 'Since' is used with a starting point in time.

questions.q: Which word means the same as 'begin'?
questions.e: Begin and start are synonyms.

questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.e: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.q: 'Quickly' is which part of speech?
questions.e: It describes how an action is done, so it is an adverb.

questions.q: What is the opposite of 'generous'?
questions.e: Generous means giving freely; selfish is the opposite.

questions.q: The book ___ on the table.
questions.e: 'The book' is singular, so use 'is'.

questions.q: Which word means 'a short story with a moral'?
questions.e: Fables like Aesop's are short stories that teach a lesson.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ honest man.
questions.e: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

questions.q: They ___ playing football now.
questions.e: 'They' takes 'are' in the present continuous.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'difficult'?
questions.e: Difficult and hard both mean not easy.

questions.q: Which of these is a preposition?
questions.e: 'Under' shows position or relation, so it is a preposition.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: He has ___ his homework.
questions.e: After 'has', use the past participle: finished.

subjects.name: Logical Reasoning
subjects.desc: Number series, patterns and the kind of thinking exams test.

questions.q: What comes next: 2, 4, 6, 8, ?
questions.e: The series adds 2 each time.

questions.q: What comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, ?
questions.e: These are perfect squares: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5².

questions.q: Odd one out: dog, cat, cow, rose
questions.e: The others are animals; rose is a plant.

questions.q: What comes next: A, C, E, G, ?
questions.e: Skip one letter each time: A, C, E, G, I.

questions.q: If today is Monday, what day is it after 10 days?
questions.e: 10 days = 7 + 3, so Monday plus 3 days is Thursday.

questions.q: What comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
questions.e: Each number doubles.

questions.q: Which number is missing: 5, 10, 20, ?, 80
questions.e: Each number doubles, so 20 × 2 = 40.

questions.q: Odd one out: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9
questions.e: All are prime numbers except 9 (3 × 3).

questions.q: If A=1, B=2, C=3, what is CAB?
Ram is taller than Sam. Sam is taller than Tom. Who is the shortest?
questions.e: Tom is shorter than Sam, and Sam is shorter than Ram.

questions.q: What is 20% of 150?
What comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.e: Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so next is +12 = 42.

questions.q: Odd one out: square, circle, triangle, cube
questions.e: A cube is 3D; the others are flat 2D shapes.

questions.q: What comes next: Z, X, V, T, ?
questions.e: Skip one letter backwards: Z, X, V, T, R.

questions.q: If you rearrange the letters of LISTEN, you get:
questions.e: Listen can become silent, enlist or tinsel.

questions.q: 5 machines make 5 items in 5 minutes. How long do 100 machines take to make 100 items?
questions.e: Each machine makes one item in 5 minutes, so 100 machines still need 5 minutes.

questions.q: What comes next: 100, 50, 25, ?
questions.e: Each number is halved, so 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5.

questions.q: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. What is C to A?
questions.e: C is A's child, but the gender is not given.

questions.q: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Therefore:
questions.e: The two statements do not tell us anything about roses specifically.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:00?
questions.e: At 3:00 the hour hand points at 3 and the minute hand at 12 — a right angle.

subjects.name: Space & Astronomy
subjects.desc: Planets, missions and the scale of the universe around us.

questions.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.e: Iron oxide (rust) on the surface gives Mars its red colour.

questions.q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.e: Jupiter is more massive than all the other planets combined.

questions.q: What is the Sun?
questions.e: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

questions.q: Which planet has the most prominent rings?
questions.e: Saturn's rings are the brightest and most visible from Earth.

questions.q: What is Earth's natural satellite?
questions.e: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.e: Light takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to travel from Sun to Earth.

questions.q: Which was the first artificial satellite?
questions.e: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957.

questions.q: Who was the first human in space?
questions.e: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in 1961.

questions.q: What was India's first satellite?
questions.e: Aryabhata was launched in 1975.

questions.q: In which year did Chandrayaan-3 land on the Moon?
questions.e: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.

questions.q: What is a light year a measure of?
questions.e: A light year is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest in the solar system?
questions.e: Venus has a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat.

questions.q: Which galaxy do we live in?
questions.e: Our solar system sits inside the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: What is a black hole?
o: A region whose gravity is so strong light cannot escape
questions.e: Nothing that crosses its event horizon can escape.

questions.q: What does ISRO stand for?
questions.e: ISRO is India's national space agency.

questions.q: Which planet rotates almost on its side?
questions.e: Uranus is tilted about 98 degrees, so it appears to roll around the Sun.

questions.q: The asteroid belt lies between which two planets?
questions.e: Most asteroids orbit between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.e: There are 8 planets since Pluto was reclassified in 2006.

questions.q: Which star is closest to Earth?
questions.e: The Sun is our nearest star.

questions.q: What is the name of the force that keeps planets in orbit?
questions.e: Gravity holds planets in orbit around the Sun.
